summary: Mistral introduced Robostral Navigate, an 8B in-house robotics navigation model that uses a single RGB camera (no depth sensors or LiDAR) to follow language instructions, reporting 76.6% success on the R2R-CE unseen benchmark and describing a prefix-caching training method that cuts training tokens 22x plus an online RL stage using CISPO.

mechanisms.reason: The model demonstrates a first-of-kind result: single-camera navigation matching or beating multi-sensor systems, a step-change in the embodied navigation task class.
mechanisms.quote: Consequently, it beats the best single-camera approach by 9.7 points and the best system using depth or multiple cameras by 4.5 points, despite using neither.

practices.reason: A specialized navigation model with stated SOTA results on a standard benchmark is worth investigating for robotics/embodied use cases, though not a dimension most software teams currently build on.
practices.quote: Robostral Navigate uses only one ordinary RGB camera and no depth sensors, yet still achieves 76.6% on R2R-CE (Room-to-Room in Continuous Environments) validation unseen

practices.reason: The document reports standard navigation benchmark metrics (Success Rate, SPL, Navigation Error) that are the lab's own internal evaluation process for a niche domain, not broadly transferable.
practices.quote: Success Rate Oracle Success Rate Success weighted by path length Navigation Error
